About the DLF Forum

About the Conference

DLF programs stretch year-round, but we are perhaps best known for our signature event, the annual DLF Forum. The DLF Forum welcomes digital library, archives, and museum practitioners from member institutions and beyond—for whom it serves as a meeting place, marketplace, and congress. As a meeting place, the DLF Forum provides an opportunity for our Advisory Committee, working groups, and community members to conduct their business and present their work. As a marketplace, the Forum provides an opportunity for community members to share experiences and practices with one another and support a broader level of information sharing among professional staff. As a congress, the Forum provides an opportunity for the DLF to continually review and assess its programs and its progress with input from the community at large.

Here, the DLF community celebrates successes, learns from mistakes, sets grassroots agendas, and organizes for action.

Save the Date

The 2021 DLF Forum and affiliated events, including NDSA's Digital Preservation 2021, will be held online November 1-4 and 8-10!

Check out our past DLF Forums and subscribe to our Forum News mailing list for information and important updates.

Code of Conduct

The Digital Library Federation (DLF) is committed to creating and supporting inclusive, diverse, and equitable communities of practice. We strive to be a welcoming organization and the focal point for a digital library culture that is anti-oppression, recognizes intersectionalities, and works compassionately across difference. Together, DLF members advance research, learning, social justice, and the public good through the creative design and wise application of digital library technologies. We know that the best problem-solving and critical thinking happens when people with a wide array of experiences and perspectives come together to work in comfort and safety as peers.

We therefore expect participants in the DLF community to help create thoughtful and respectful environments where that interaction can take place.

Please review our DLF Code of Conduct prior to joining us at the Forum.

We're so grateful to our community

Thank you

The 2021 DLF Forum and Learn@DLF are community and practitioner-based events that would not be possible without thoughtful and engaged participation from our community. We especially thank our 2021 DLF Forum Planning Committee.

item.title: thank you
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
We're so grateful to our community

Thank you

The 2021 DLF Forum and Learn@DLF are community and practitioner-based events that would not be possible without thoughtful and engaged participation from our community. We especially thank our 2021 DLF Forum Planning Committee.

item.title: homepage-2021-06-01
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
A world-class marketplace of ideas for digital GLAM practitioners since 1999

What's the DLF Forum?

DLF programs stretch year-round, but we are perhaps best known for our signature event, the annual DLF Forum. The DLF Forum welcomes digital library, archives, and museum practitioners from member institutions and beyond—for whom it serves as a meeting place, marketplace, and congress.

Learn about the event and plan to attend

Attend our Affiliated Events!

NDSA's Digital Preservation 2021

November 4

Digital Preservation is the annual conference of the National Digital Stewardship Alliance. DigiPres is expected to be a crucial venue for intellectual exchange, community-building, development of best practices, and national-level agenda-setting in the field.

Learn@DLF

November 8-10

Now in its fourth year, Learn@DLF returns in 2021 includes engaging, hands-on sessions where attendees will gain experience with new tools and resources, exchange ideas, and develop and share expertise with fellow community members as well as short tutorials about specific tools, techniques, workflows, or concepts.

Make an Impact!

Sponsor the DLF Forum and NDSA's #DigiPres21

DLF Forum starts in

Days Hours Minutes Seconds NOW

What makes the DLF Forum great?

After nearly 14 years of academic library experience and subsequently participating in no less than 25 conferences, I can say that the DLF Forum was the most progressive and enlightening conference that I have ever attended. It was downright empowering. Ana Ndumu 2017 DLF Forum Fellow The thoughtful way the experience was designed was due to the efforts of the organizers...As a first-time participant, I am grateful to have been able to participate in this year’s virtual Forum and look forward to continuing to learn from the DLF community! Betsy Yoon 2020 DLF Forum Community Journalist

Forum Updates

item.title: homepage-2021-06-01
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
A world-class marketplace of ideas for digital GLAM practitioners since 1999

What's the DLF Forum?

DLF programs stretch year-round, but we are perhaps best known for our signature event, the annual DLF Forum. The DLF Forum welcomes digital library, archives, and museum practitioners from member institutions and beyond—for whom it serves as a meeting place, marketplace, and congress.

Learn about the event and plan to attend

Attend our Affiliated Events!

NDSA's Digital Preservation 2021

November 4

Digital Preservation is the annual conference of the National Digital Stewardship Alliance. DigiPres is expected to be a crucial venue for intellectual exchange, community-building, development of best practices, and national-level agenda-setting in the field.

Learn@DLF

November 8-10

Now in its fourth year, Learn@DLF returns in 2021 includes engaging, hands-on sessions where attendees will gain experience with new tools and resources, exchange ideas, and develop and share expertise with fellow community members as well as short tutorials about specific tools, techniques, workflows, or concepts.

Make an Impact!

Sponsor the DLF Forum and NDSA's #DigiPres21

DLF Forum starts in

Days Hours Minutes Seconds NOW

What makes the DLF Forum great?

After nearly 14 years of academic library experience and subsequently participating in no less than 25 conferences, I can say that the DLF Forum was the most progressive and enlightening conference that I have ever attended. It was downright empowering. Ana Ndumu 2017 DLF Forum Fellow The thoughtful way the experience was designed was due to the efforts of the organizers...As a first-time participant, I am grateful to have been able to participate in this year’s virtual Forum and look forward to continuing to learn from the DLF community! Betsy Yoon 2020 DLF Forum Community Journalist

Forum Updates

item.title: homepage-2021-06-01
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
A world-class marketplace of ideas for digital GLAM practitioners since 1999

What's the DLF Forum?

DLF programs stretch year-round, but we are perhaps best known for our signature event, the annual DLF Forum. The DLF Forum welcomes digital library, archives, and museum practitioners from member institutions and beyond—for whom it serves as a meeting place, marketplace, and congress.

Learn about the event and plan to attend

Attend our Affiliated Events!

NDSA's Digital Preservation 2021

November 4

Digital Preservation is the annual conference of the National Digital Stewardship Alliance. DigiPres is expected to be a crucial venue for intellectual exchange, community-building, development of best practices, and national-level agenda-setting in the field.

Learn@DLF

November 8-10

Now in its fourth year, Learn@DLF returns in 2021 includes engaging, hands-on sessions where attendees will gain experience with new tools and resources, exchange ideas, and develop and share expertise with fellow community members as well as short tutorials about specific tools, techniques, workflows, or concepts.

Make an Impact!

Sponsor the DLF Forum and NDSA's #DigiPres21

DLF Forum starts in

Days Hours Minutes Seconds NOW

What makes the DLF Forum great?

After nearly 14 years of academic library experience and subsequently participating in no less than 25 conferences, I can say that the DLF Forum was the most progressive and enlightening conference that I have ever attended. It was downright empowering. Ana Ndumu 2017 DLF Forum Fellow The thoughtful way the experience was designed was due to the efforts of the organizers...As a first-time participant, I am grateful to have been able to participate in this year’s virtual Forum and look forward to continuing to learn from the DLF community! Betsy Yoon 2020 DLF Forum Community Journalist

Forum Updates

item.title: sp-section-2
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
2021 Sponsorship Opportunities

In 2020, the first fully virtual DLF Forum and NDSA’s Digital Preservation welcomed over 2,000 individuals from all 50 states, Washington, DC, Puerto Rico, and over 30 different countries, with nearly 1,200 people viewing the Forum’s opening plenary.

This year, our social-first, accessible, and inclusive virtual platform provides the opportunity to have scheduled and spontaneous interactions with conference attendees. Custom video booths, targeted branding placements, and low-cost registration give you the chance to participate and learn what is resonating with conference attendees and the organizations they represent.

item.title: Sponsorship Opportunity Header
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
Sponsorship Opportunities

Be a 2021 Events Sponsor!

Sponsor the 2021 DLF Forum and NDSA’s Digital Preservation and get ready to engage with thousands of decision-makers in the fields of libraries, digitization, and preservation.

2021 Sponsorship Opportunities

In 2020, the first fully virtual DLF Forum and NDSA’s Digital Preservation welcomed over 2,000 individuals from all 50 states, Washington, DC, Puerto Rico, and over 30 different countries, with nearly 1,200 people viewing the Forum’s opening plenary.

This year, our social-first, accessible, and inclusive virtual platform provides the opportunity to have scheduled and spontaneous interactions with conference attendees. Custom video booths, targeted branding placements, and low-cost registration give you the chance to participate and learn what is resonating with conference attendees and the organizations they represent.

Premier

ONLY ONE PREMIER SPONSOR AVAILABLE $ 7,000
  • Event platform branding
  • Host attendee event
  • Direct emails to attendees (2)
  • Video ads between events
  • Custom header in all event emails
  • Custom virtual sponsor booth
  • Logo in event communications
  • Logo featured on event website
  • Custom posts on social media
  • Logo featured on platform log on
Be the Premier Sponsor Exclusive

Platinum

ENGAGE WITH ATTENDEES $ 3,750
  • Direct emails to attendees (1)
  • Video ads between events
  • Custom banner in event emails (3)
  • Custom virtual sponsor booth
  • Logo in event communications
  • Logo featured on event website
  • Custom posts on social media
  • Logo featured on platform log on
Be a Platinum Sponsor

Gold

SHOW YOUR SUPPORT $ 1,500
  • Custom banner in one event email
  • Custom virtual sponsor booth
  • Logo in event communications
  • Logo featured on event website

  • Logo featured on platform log on

Unique and Custom Sponsor Opportunities

Looking for something unique or custom? We are here to create an opportunity that is meaningful for your organization and our attendees. Sponsorship of our events is always a collaborative process.

item.title: Sponsor Level Pages Template
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
Sponsorship Opportunities

Premier Sponsor

As the Premier Sponsor your organization will support the social-first, accessible, and inclusive virtual platform that will connect our presenters, attendees, and other sponsors. Submit the following form for more information or to let us know that you are ready to be our premier sponsor.

Premier

ONLY ONE PREMIER SPONSOR AVAILABLE $ 7,000
  • Event platform branding
  • Host attendee event
  • Direct emails to attendees (2)
  • Video ads between events
  • Custom header in all event emails
  • Custom virtual sponsor booth
  • Logo in event communications
  • Logo featured on event website
  • Custom posts on social media
  • Logo featured on platform log on page
2021 DLF Forum & NDSA's Digital Preservation Exclusive

Premier Sponsor Interest Form

item.title: schedule blocks
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
Schedule

About the Conference

DLF programs stretch year-round, but we are perhaps best known for our signature event, the annual DLF Forum. The DLF Forum welcomes digital library, archives, and museum practitioners from member institutions and beyond—for whom it serves as a meeting place, marketplace, and congress. As a meeting place, the DLF Forum provides an opportunity for our Advisory Committee, working groups, and community members to conduct their business and present their work. As a marketplace, the Forum provides an opportunity for community members to share experiences and practices with one another and support a broader level of information sharing among professional staff. As a congress, the Forum provides an opportunity for the DLF to continually review and assess its programs and its progress with input from the community at large.

Here, the DLF community celebrates successes, learns from mistakes, sets grassroots agendas, and organizes for action.

  • DLF Forum - Day 1 - Monday, November 1
  • Social/Wellness/Networking Events - 10-11am ET
  • Opening Plenary - 11am-1pm ET
  • Birds of a Feather Sessions - 1-2pm ET

1. Weaving Knowledge Networks

2. Failure Is an Option

3. Not Doing More with Less

  • 1:00 - 1:30
  • [SPEAKERS]

4. Community-Built Accessibility

5. Building for Tomorrow

6. Teach Me about the Anthropocene

  • 1:30 - 2:00
  • [SPEAKERS]
  • Break - 2-2:30pm ET
  • Track 1
  • Track 2

Protecting readers' right to privacy in single-sign-on access

  • 2:30 - 3:15pm ET
  • [speakers]

CLIR/HBCU Library Alliance Partner Session 1

  • 2:30 - 3:15pm ET
  • [speakers]
  • Break - 3:15-3:30pm ET
  • DLF Working Group Meetups - 3:30-4:15pm

1. Assessment Interest Group (AIG)

2. Digital Library Pedagogy Group (#DLFteach)

3. DLF Committee for Equity & Inclusion (DLF-CEI)

3. Born-Digital Access Working Group

  • Break - 4:15-4:30pm ET

Access, Accountability, Action

  • 4:30 - 5:15pm ET
  • [speakers]

Stories From the Inside: Documenting Incarcerated People’s Experiences During the COVID-19 Pandemic

  • 4:30 - 5:15pm ET
  • [speakers]
  • Break - 5:15-5:30pm ET
  • Lightning Talks - 5:30-6:30pm ET

1. Falling Through the Cracks: Metadata inadequacies for rock climbing

2. Infusing Critical Evaluation of Data Visualizations in Open and Tool-centric Workshops

3. Community Collaboration, Scalability, and Digitization During an Unprecedented Time

4. Digital Humanities, in the Year of the Plague: Library Support of DH Projects During the COVID-19 Pandemic

5. Explore the New Season of CLIR's Material Memory Podcast

6. The Marmaduke Problem: Comics, Linked Data, and Community-led Authority Control

7. Remediating Harmful Language and Content in Digital Archives

8. An Evolving Approach to Mass Digitization: Arabic Collections Online

9. A Pedagogy of Digital Infrastructures: Usability and Pandemic-Inflected Experiential Learning

  • [SPEAKERS]

Hurry up & reserve your spot!

Learn new skills and get insights from experts and practitioners from all around!

Register today

item.title: keynote
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
Dr. Nikole Hannah-Jones

Dr. Nikole Hannah-Jones

Nikole Hannah-Jones is the Pulitzer Prize-winning creator of the 1619 Project and a staff writer at The New York Times Magazine. She has spent her career investigating racial inequality and injustice, and her reporting has earned her the MacArthur Fellowship, known as the Genius grant, a Peabody Award, two George Polk Awards and the National Magazine Award three times. Hannah-Jones also earned the John Chancellor Award for Distinguished Journalism and was named Journalist of the Year by the National Association of Black Journalists and the Newswomen's Club of New York. In 2020 she was inducted into the Society of American Historians and in 2021, into the North Carolina Media Hall of Fame.

In 2016, Hannah-Jones co-founded the Ida B. Wells Society for Investigative Reporting, which seeks to increase the number of reporters and editors of color. She holds a Master of Arts in Mass Communication from the University of North Carolina and earned her Bachelor of Arts in History and African-American studies from the University of Notre Dame.

Hannah-Jones is the Knight Chair in Race and Journalism at Howard University, where she has founded the Center for Journalism & Democracy.

item.title: FAQ
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
I only registered for DLF Forum. Can I attend the other events (NDSA's DigiPres and Learn@DLF)?

If you only reserved a ticket for DLF Forum, that ticket is only for that event. If you’d like to attend NDSA’s Digital Preservation or any of the Learn@DLF workshops (priced at $35 each), please reserve tickets for those events. 

Where are these events taking place?

All events are virtual and will utilize the conference platform Midspace (formerly Clowdr). After registration, you will receive instructions for signing up for Midspace. 

DLF Forum and NDSA's DigiPres are free with option to donate. For what purpose are donations collected?

Any donations collected will go toward offsetting costs of the conference platform and supporting conference programs such as the Community Journalist fellowship.

item.title: 2022-keynote-speaker
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
2022 DLF Forum Keynote Speaker

David Neimer, PhD

David Nemer is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Media Studies and in the Latin American Studies program at the University of Virginia. He is also a Faculty Associate at Harvard University's Berkman Klein Center and Princeton University's Brazil Lab. Nemer is the author of Technology of the Oppressed (MIT Press, 2022) and Favela Digital: The other side of technology (Editora GSA, 2013). He holds a MA in Anthropology from the University of Virginia and a Ph.D. in Computing, Culture, and Society from Indiana University. Nemer has written for The Guardian, El País, The Huffington Post (HuffPost), Salon, and The Intercept.

item.title: 2022 Local Guide
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
Local Guide: Baltimore MD

Table of Contents

CLIR Events Local Guide to Baltimore 2022

Thank you to the 2022 DLF Forum Community Committee for authoring this guide, and to the DLF Digital Accessibility Working Group for reviewing and testing for accessibility.

Prepare for your visit to Baltimore

Review the weather forecast:
October weather is kind of a crapshoot - it could be really hot or really cold! We suggest checking a few days before you leave to decide what to pack. So far the prediction is some crisp, fall weather in the low 50s to mid 60s. Could rain, but not likely (averaging 4 inches for the month).

Discover some Baltimore-focused resources:

  • Download the Explore Baltimore Heritage app.
  • Guide to Black-owned businesses
  • Guide to Indigenous Baltimore - Chronicles the history and heritage of East Baltimore’s Historic American Indian “Reservation” in the 20th Century.
  • Fell’s Point neighborhood guide


Listen to Baltimore podcasts:

  • Maryland Curiosity Bureau
  • Rise of Charm City
  • Out of the Blocks


Listen to the DLF community-made Baltimore-themed Spotify playlist:

[iframe src="https://open.spotify.com/embed/playlist/7j4W7YK8UzRcZAB6DcD4cC?utm_source=generator" width="100%" height="380" frameBorder="0"]

How to get to the hotel and get around

Getting to the hotel: If you are flying into BWI, we recommend taking the Light Raillink to the Pratt Street stop, and then follow Pratt east for a half mile to the hotel at 202 E Pratt Street.

Parking: Parking is available at the hotel for $32-$35 per day to self-park. Valet parking at a higher rate is also available. There are several parking garages within a couple of blocks that run from around $25-$35 per day. Parking around town is often street parking. It's often difficult on the weekends to find parking in the Fell’s Point and Federal Hill neighborhoods, but in most other neighborhoods it’s fine.

Getting Around: Baltimore is a city of neighborhoods and is pretty car-centric. That being said, there are public transportation options by land and water. The Charm City Circulator and the Harbor Connector Ferry are free!

The Light Rail Link on Pratt Street is a great option for traveling along the north-south corridor of the city with stops in Mount Vernon, Hampden, Woodberry, and Camden Yards.

Accessibility: In general, the Inner Harbor area near the hotel is wheelchair accessible, though sidewalks may be hit-or-miss. Businesses in old rowhomes in neighborhoods such as Fell’s Point, Federal Hill, and Hampden may not be wheelchair accessible. We recommend exploring Baltimore through this wheelchair accessible travel guide. Accessibility tags throughout this guide are based on Yelp reviews. Menu accessibility is based on testing with a screen reader.

Explore

[iframe src="https://www.google.com/maps/d/embed?mid=1rZei19oRPgeJz41xj96OnDyqdhMr2Lla&ehbc=2E312F"]

Where to Eat

Within .5 miles of the hotel Local fast food nearby hotel Farther out but awesome Ice Cream Within .5 miles of the hotel

La Calle: (0.2 miles) “Modern” Mexican. Lunch and dinner. Menu not accessible.

Pitamore: (0.2 miles) Mediterranean; amazing Shawarma and falafel: good for lunch and early dinner (closes at 6pm); Yelp: $; also has options and labels for gluten-free, vegan, and vegetarian. Menu partially accessible.

Miss Shirley’s Cafe: (0.3 miles) Maryland Southern food focused on using local ingredients. Breakfast, brunch, and lunch; Yelp $$; can have very long wait times, especially on the weekends. Menu accessible. Wheelchair accessible.

Blackwall Hitch: (0.3 miles) Great happy hour. Open for lunch and dinner. Menu accessible.

Ramen Utsuke: (0.4 miles) Ramen and Sushi. Vegan and vegetarian options. Wheelchair accessible. Menu not accessible.

Liora: (0.4 miles) Plant-based and locally sourced fine dining. Wheelchair accessible. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Menu somewhat accessible on mobile.

Local fast food nearby hotel

Shake Shack: (350 feet) Originally started in NYC, but you can’t beat burgers, fries, and milkshakes.

Royal Farms: (0.2 miles) Call it RoFo to sound like a local. Fried chicken is their specialty. Menu minimally accessible.

Hip Hop Fish & Chicken: (0.2 miles) Fried chicken and lake trout, catfish – southern. Menu accessible.

Farther out but awesome

Little Italy: Where Nancy Pelosi grew up (check out the bocce courts at D’Alesandro Park on Stiles Street–named after her father); super cute neighborhood close to hotel with tons of places to eat, but in particular faves:

Vaccaro’s: (0.5 miles) Delicious Italian cookies and pastries. Wheelchair accessible. Menu not accessible.
Ovenbird: (0.6 miles) Bakery with wonderful bread. Wheelchair accessible. Menu not accessible.
Amicci’s: (0.6 miles) Gluten-free pasta options. Lunch and dinner and a great happy hour. Menu accessible.
Angeli’s Pizzeria: (0.7 miles) Vegan and gluten-free pizza options! Lunch and dinner. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.

Forno: (0.7 miles) Italian wine bar; good happy hour available Tuesday – Friday 3pm – 6pm at the Bar, Market, & Patio; lunch and dinner. Gluten-free pasta and pizza available. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.

Watersong Yunnan Kitchen: (0.9 miles) Hidden gem in the Federal Hill neighborhood. Get the mushrooms and baked tilapia! BYOB. Asian-owned. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.

Lexington Market: (1 mile) Since 1782, America’s largest, continuously operating market. Recent renovation opening in fall of 2022, but many of its vendors are still open right now. Including world-famous crab cakes from Faidley’s.

Mount Vernon Marketplace: (1 mile) A wide variety of restaurants and bars within one building, including The Local Oyster featuring the Colossal Crab Sandwich as seen on Netflix. Menu minimally accessible.

Trinacria Foods: (1.1 miles) One of the oldest operating Italian delis and run by the same family (opened in 1908), Italian food products for sale including amazing and affordable wine, sandwiches, soup, salads. Great gluten-free options! Best for lunch takeout. Menu accessible.

Cocina Luchadores: (1.4 miles) Order at the counter at this family-run restaurant serving Mexican street foods and breakfast items. Menu accessible.

Papi Cuisine: (1.5 miles) Caribbean fusion style cuisine and cocktails. Black-owned business. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Wheelchair accessible. Menu not accessible.

Johnny Rad’s: (1.5 miles) Artisanal pizza, eclectic pub fare & a variety of beer are offered in casual digs with arcade games by Patterson Park. Vegan friendly. Menu accessible.

Locust Point Steamers (“LP Steamers”): (1.7 miles) This seafood joint is informal, affordable, and delicious! Set inside a rowhome, family-owned. Great place to get a dozen crabs and a Natty Boh or two. Rooftop seating available if not too cold. Menu not accessible.

Clavel: (3.0 miles) Popular mezcaleria and taqueria located in the Remington neighborhood. Happy Hour is Monday-Friday, 5-7pm; $4 off Margaritas and Queso Fundido (both amazingly delicious). Latine-owned. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Wheelchair accessible. Menu minimally accessible. Pro-tip: get drinks at nearby WC Harlan while you wait for your table. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Menu accessible.

Blue Pit BBQ & Whiskey Bar: (3.9 miles) Delicious BBQ spot in the Hampden neighborhood. Limited gluten-free, vegan, and vegetarian options. Easy to access via Light Raillink, Woodberry stop. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.

Franchesca’s Empanadas Cafe: Cafe in Highlandtown neighborhood serving meat and vegan empanadas! Woman-owned. Menu accessible.

Dylan’s Oyster Cellar: (4.1 miles) Restaurant in the Hampden neighborhood that offers a fantastic selection of all types of seafood, but they also have a great burger and unique cocktails. Also recommend trying a Baltimore staple, the Coddie (codfish cake, usually served with saltines). Gender-neutral bathrooms. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.

Koko’s Pub: (5.5 miles) Crab cakes! Menu accessible.

Ekiben: (1.1 miles) No-frills Asian spot with a focus on unusual steamed buns, plus bowls & small plates. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Menu accessible.

Ice Cream

The Charmery: (various) Lots of locally inspired flavors from this husband and wife team, like Lemon Stick and Old Bay Caramel, along with the classics (and a few dairy-free options). There are multiple locations: the closest to the hotel is 0.8 miles away but open seasonally (wheelchair accessible), and there is another in the Hampden neighborhood open more regularly, 3.6 miles away (gender-neutral bathrooms).

Cajou Creamery: (0.9 miles) Only open Friday-Sunday, serves delicious plant-based ice cream. Black-owned business. Vegan. Menu accessible.

Taharka Brothers Ice Cream- R.House: (3.6 miles) or Cross Street Market (0.9 miles). Local employee-owned ice cream company that serves amazing small-batch ice cream. Limited vegan options. Majority black-owned business. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.

Bmore Licks: (0.6) in Federal Hill or (1.8) miles by Patterson Park. Over 100 flavors of hand-made soft-serve ice cream. Gender-neutral restrooms. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.

Hecho En Baltimore: (2.3 miles) for paletas (an amazing Mexican frozen dessert) and products made by local artisans.

Pitango Gelato: (.6 mi) in Federal Hill; made on premises gelato and sorbet desserts. Well worth the short walk.

Where to Drink

Coffee Tea Breweries Bars Coffee

Most of the best local coffee places are not near the hotel, but there is a Starbucks inside the hotel.

3 Bean Coffee: (0.6 miles) Serves Vagrant coffee. Grab a to-go cup and see the views from nearby Federal Hill Park. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Wheelchair accessible. No online menu.

Ceremony Coffee: (0.9 miles at the Cross Street Market) Menu not accessible. Grab a breakfast sammy at Steve’s lunch stall while you’re there, a staple of SoBo for the past 50 years, or a cold press juice or smoothie at Gangster Vegan Organics.

Dooby’s: (1 mile away) Check out this Korean-inspired cafe in the Mount Vernon neighborhood for breakfast and Passenger coffee. Asian-owned. Gender-neutral restrooms. Wheel-chair accessible. Menu accessible.

Sophomore Coffee (2.2 miles away) Small gem of a coffee shop with great espresso. Woman and Black owned. Menu not accessible.

Café Los Sueños: (2.8 miles) Cozy coffee shop in the Remington neighborhood. The owner grew up working in the coffee fields of El Salvador and roasts their own beans. No online menu.

Dovecote Cafe: (3.0 miles) Gorgeous community-centric cafe in the Reservoir Hill neighborhood with a creative menu and events. Black-owned and women-owned. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Wheelchair accessible. No online menu.

Good Neighbor: (4 miles) In Hampden. Great coffee drinks, sandwiches and pastries, along with a curated selection of home goods and kitchen/bar staples. Amazing and large outdoor space and seating, including Green Neighbor, their plant shop. Gender-neutral restrooms. No online menu.

Artifact Coffee: (4 miles) Rustic coffeehouse in a reclaimed factory building serving locally sourced and seasonal light bites. Located in the Hampden/Woodberry neighborhood near Waverly Brewing, Accessible from Light Raillink Woodberry Stop. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Wheelchair accessible. Menu not accessible.

Tea

Cuples Tea House: (0.9 miles) Open Wednesday to Saturday. Loose-teas and teawares for purchase, along with tea prepared and served in a cozy setting with some prepared sandwiches, pastries, etc. Black/Woman owned small business. Menu minimally accessible.

Teavolve Cafe: (1.1 miles) Harbor East’s favorite cafe to enjoy a colorful menu rich with plant-based and GF options. Black/Woman owned small business. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Menu not accessible.

Corner Juice Bar: (2.0 miles) Open Tuesday to Sunday. Healthy and delicious juices made to order! Order a juice and stroll Patterson Park. Menu accessible.

Breweries

A comprehensive guide

Checkerspot: (1.2 miles) Woman-owned and brewed gluten-reduced beers. Dog-friendly. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.

Ministry of Brewing: (1.2 miles) Spacious brewery in Upper Fells Point housed in the former St. Michael’s Church. Wheelchair accessible. Menu not accessible.

Suspended Brewing Company: (1.2 miles) Women of color-owned vegan, cruelty-free mixed fermentation beers in Pigtown. Wheelchair accessible. Stop by the B&O Railroad Museum while you’re in the area. No online menu.

Charm City Meadworks: (1.2 miles) 20 minutes by bus or 7 minutes by car. Large taproom with indoor and outdoor seating serving locally made mead (gluten-free). Bring your own food. Dog-friendly. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Wheelchair accessible. Menu minimally accessible.

Diamondback Brewery: (1.9 miles) Unfiltered lagers, hop-forward ales, and mixed fermentation brews. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.

Monument City Brewery: (3.0 miles) Well-considered, drinkable ales designed to be a go-to beer choice. Dogs allowed. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.

Bars

The Owl Bar inside the Belvedere Hotel (on the first floor): (1.3 miles) a favorite of H.L. Menken and F. Scott Fitzgerald and other celebrities of their day. A quote from Fitzgerald on Baltimore: “I belong here, where everything is civilized and gay and rotted and polite.” Menu minimally accessible.

Sugarvale (1 mile): A cozy cocktail bar in the Mount Vernon neighborhood with great ambience. Limited indoor seating and vaccination cards required. Gender-neutral restrooms. Menu not accessible.

Fadensonnen: (2.2 miles) 20 minutes by bus or 11 minutes by car. An upscale beer garden and tavern in the artsy Station North neighborhood focusing on ethically produced beer, wine, nihonshu, and shochu. Generous outdoor seating. Women-owned. Gender-neutral restrooms. Menu accessible.

Dutch Courage: (2.2 miles) Fantastic gin bar and a great back up if Fadensonnen is crowded. Menu not accessible.

WC Harlan: (3 miles) Bar in Remington serving speakeasy style cocktails and drinks. Note: There is no sign, search for the black door that has “Enter” written in chalk. Gender-neutral restrooms. Menu accessible.

Club Charles: (aka Club Chuck) (2.2. miles) One of John Waters’ favorites, a divine divey bar with a jukebox, cheap drinks, and fun bathroom graffiti. Menu not available.

Bluebird Cocktail Room: (4.0 miles) Romantic, literary-themed cocktail bar in the Hampden neighborhood. Gender-neutral restrooms. Menu not accessible.

Melanie’s at Griffith’s Tavern: (4.0 miles) LGBTQ and women owned Hampden neighborhood dive bar with reasonably priced drinks. Menu not available.

Where to Visit

Since you’re at the Inner Harbor, visit the National Aquarium (wheelchair accessible), Turtle Island, and local celebrity Mr. Trash Wheel at his home 0.6 miles away. This googly eyed genius keeps our bay clean and encourages recycling. Tag him on social media (seriously his Instagram is one of the best). He is related to Professor Trash Wheel, Captain Trash Wheel, and Gwynnda the Good Wheel of the West, but he was the first. He has also partnered with local brewery Peabody Heights on 3 beers, Solar Power Sour, Lost Python Ale (from that time when a python came to visit with the trash), and Professor Trash Wheel Blinded Me With Science.

See the Reginald F. Lewis Museum of African American History (0.4 miles) and The National Great Blacks in Wax Museum (2.5 miles)

See Edgar Allen Poe’s grave (0.9 miles) at 515 W Fayette St, a 17-minute walk; open during the day, and then go see his house and museum (1.5 miles). The house is not wheel-chair accessible but the museum is.

Jewish Museum of Maryland: (0.7 miles) near Attman’s Deli and includes historic Lloyd Street Synagogue. Get corned beef on Corned Beef Row at Attman’s Deli for lunch.

See outsider art at the American Visionary Art Museum (1.2 miles) and some amazing letter presses at the Baltimore Museum of Industry, located in a former oyster cannery (1.5 miles). Grab some seafood at nearby LP Steamers and a beer at Diamondback brewery. Both wheelchair accessible.

For fine and contemporary art, visit the Walters (0.9 miles) and the Baltimore Museum of Art (3.0 miles), both free and conveniently located along the Light Rail. Both wheelchair accessible. For local galleries, Galerie Myrtis (2.1 miles) is Black, woman-owned blue-chip gallery specializing in twentieth and twenty-first-century American art with a focus on work created by African American artists.

For a bibliophile tour, visit the Enoch Pratt Free Library (0.8 miles), the recently renovated central branch, as well as the George Peabody Library (0.9 miles). Known as Baltimore’s “Cathedral of Books,” Peabody is consistently ranked among the most beautiful libraries in the world. If it happens to be the one day of the month that Book Thing (2.9 miles) is open, trek up to Charles Village to pick up some free collaging gems. All wheelchair accessible. Nearby is worker-owned Red Emma’s Bookstore Coffeehouse and Normals Books & Records.

What to Do

Stroll along the Promenade - the brick route along the Baltimore Harbor. Head toward Federal Hill (to the right when you’re facing the water and the hotel is at your back) or Fells Point and Canton (to the left). There’s a pleasant path along the water for several miles in each direction from the hotel. Most parts of the Promenade are wheelchair, bike, and stroller accessible. Learn more about the Promenade and view maps on the Baltimore City website.

Go on a Saturday morning to the Waverly Farmer’s Market or on a Sunday morning to the Baltimore Farmers Market under I-83. See the Hollywood Diner from the Barry Levinson movies “Diner” and “Tin Men” (0.5 miles) at Holliday and Saratoga Sts.: not a restaurant anymore. See it in the 1980s as the Kids Diner.

See a performance at Le Mondo (0.9 miles), an artist-owned bar and event venue with avant-garde concerts, dance, and theatrical performances.

Follow in the footsteps of Frederick Douglass around Fells Point. Do a Fells Point ghost tour (1.2 miles) and get some mussels and live music at Bertha’s across the street. Pick up the water taxi at the Fell’s Point pier for a cruise around the harbor (make sure to check out their hours since it's off season).

Do some Duckpin bowling at Patterson Bowling Center: (1.4 miles) and BYOB (Pro tip: bring a 6-pack of local brewery Union’s Duckpin Pale Ale or a pizza from Johnny Rad’s across the street)! Duckpin is like regular bowling, only smaller pins and balls, and slightly different rules–so actually, it’s pretty different. Afterwards visit Patterson Park and then go see some local art at Creative Alliance and shop at Hecho En Baltimore (2.3 miles) for paletas and products made by local artisans.

Shake and Bake Family Fun Center: (2.2 miles) Baltimore City Recreation and Parks (BCRP) owns and operates the Shake & Bake Family Fun Center in the historic Upton community in West Baltimore. “The Bake” as it is affectionately known, has been a local, iconic staple since 1982. Named after Baltimore Colts wide receiver, Glenn “Shake & Bake'' Doughty. Shake & Bake is the spot for Bowling and Roller Skating under one roof in the heart of Baltimore City! This link leads to a short video on PBS about Shake & Bake.

See a show at Ottobar (2.6 miles) and stop by Beyond Video while you’re in the neighborhood, nonprofit video rental store in a row home.

Peruse The Avenue in Hampden (3.7 miles), which is technically named W. 36th Street. Also Hampden is pronounced HAM-din. Tons of great shops (including vintage), restaurants, and bars as well as Atomic Books, an independent bookstore where John Waters gets his fan mail. Pro-tip: watch John Waters’ PECKER (1998) beforehand which takes place almost entirely in Hampden.

Lithuanian Hall: (1.2 miles) Save Your Soul is a monthly dance party featuring the best Dj's spinning the rarest and rawest Soul, RnB, and Boogaloo 45's on the first Friday of every month at the historic Lithuanian Hall in Baltimore. Try a shot of the traditional honey liqueur, Krupnikas

There are a plethora of hiking trails in and around the Baltimore area for all levels. Local favorites include the Cascade Falls Trail in Patapsco Valley State Park (21 minutes by car), the Merryman’s Mill Trail at the Loch Raven Reservoir (27 mins by car), and the Leakin Park Loop Trail up to the Orianda Mansion (21 minutes by car).

Baltimore has a number of lovely parks. Local favorites include Federal Hill Park (1 mile), Patterson Park (2.3 miles), Druid Hill (4 miles) and Clifton Park (3.1 miles).

Review the weather forecast:<\/span>
October weather is kind of a crapshoot - it could be really hot or really cold! We suggest checking a few days before you leave to decide what to pack. So far the prediction is some crisp, fall weather in the low 50s to mid 60s<\/a>. Could rain, but not likely (averaging 4 inches for the month).<\/p>

  • Download the Explore Baltimore Heritage app<\/a>.<\/li>

  • Guide to Indigenous Baltimore<\/a> - Chronicles the history and heritage of East Baltimore\u2019s Historic American Indian \u201cReservation\u201d in the 20th Century.<\/li>
  • Fell\u2019s Point neighborhood guide<\/a><\/li><\/ul>


    Listen to Baltimore podcasts:<\/span><\/p>

    • Maryland Curiosity Bureau<\/a><\/li>

    • Out of the Blocks<\/a><\/li><\/ul>

      Getting to the hotel:<\/span> If you are flying into BWI, we recommend taking the Light Raillink<\/a> to the Pratt Street stop, and then follow Pratt east for a half mile to the hotel at 202 E Pratt Street.<\/p>

      Parking:<\/span> Parking is available at the hotel for $32-$35 per day to self-park. Valet parking at a higher rate is also available. There are several parking garages within a couple of blocks that run from around $25-$35 per day. Parking around town is often street parking. It's often difficult on the weekends to find parking in the Fell\u2019s Point and Federal Hill neighborhoods, but in most other neighborhoods it\u2019s fine.<\/p>

      Getting Around:<\/span> Baltimore is a city of neighborhoods and is pretty car-centric. That being said, there are public transportation options by land<\/a> and water<\/a>. The Charm City Circulator and the Harbor Connector Ferry are free!<\/p>

      The Light Rail Link on Pratt Street is a great option for traveling along the north-south corridor of the city with stops in Mount Vernon, Hampden, Woodberry, and Camden Yards.<\/p>

      Accessibility:<\/span> In general, the Inner Harbor area near the hotel is wheelchair accessible, though sidewalks may be hit-or-miss. Businesses in old rowhomes in neighborhoods such as Fell\u2019s Point, Federal Hill, and Hampden may not be wheelchair accessible. We recommend exploring Baltimore through this wheelchair accessible travel guide<\/a>. Accessibility tags throughout this guide are based on Yelp reviews. Menu accessibility is based on testing with a screen reader.<\/p>","typography_typography":"custom","typography_font_family":"Montserrat","typography_font_weight":"500","__globals__":{"text_color":"globals\/colors?id=secondary"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"},{"id":"71a11ea1","elType":"widget","settings":{"title":"Explore","size":"xl","header_size":"h3","align":"center","__globals__":{"title_color":"globals\/colors?id=nvtextcolor"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"heading"},{"id":"7a04292e","elType":"widget","settings":{"width":{"unit":"px","size":"80","sizes":[]},"text":"Divider","weight":{"unit":"px","size":"3","sizes":[]},"align":"center","align_mobile":"left","neb_content_protection_password_placeholder":"Enter to .5 miles of the hotel","tab_content":"

      La Calle<\/a>: (0.2 miles) \u201cModern\u201d Mexican. Lunch and dinner. Menu not accessible.<\/p>

      Pitamore<\/a>: (0.2 miles) Mediterranean; amazing Shawarma and falafel: good for lunch and early dinner (closes at 6pm); Yelp: $; also has options and labels for gluten-free, vegan, and vegetarian. Menu partially accessible.<\/p>

      Miss Shirley\u2019s Cafe<\/a>: (0.3 miles) Maryland Southern food focused on using local ingredients. Breakfast, brunch, and lunch; Yelp $$; can have very long wait times, especially on the weekends. Menu accessible. Wheelchair accessible.<\/p>

      Blackwall Hitch<\/a>: (0.3 miles) Great happy hour. Open for lunch and dinner. Menu accessible.<\/p>

      Ramen Utsuke<\/a>: (0.4 miles) Ramen and Sushi. Vegan and vegetarian options. Wheelchair accessible. Menu not accessible.<\/p>

      Liora<\/a>: (0.4 miles) Plant-based and locally sourced fine dining. Wheelchair accessible. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Menu somewhat accessible on mobile.<\/p>","_id":"d16c6d3"},{"_id":"9a6f515","tab_title":"Local fast food nearby hotel","tab_content":"

      Shake Shack<\/a>: (350 feet) Originally started in NYC, but you can\u2019t beat burgers, fries, and milkshakes.<\/p>

      Royal Farms<\/a>: (0.2 miles) Call it RoFo to sound like a local. Fried chicken<\/a> is their specialty. Menu minimally accessible.<\/p>

      Hip Hop Fish & Chicken<\/a>: (0.2 miles) Fried chicken and lake trout<\/a>, catfish - southern. Menu accessible.<\/p>"},{"tab_title":"Farther out but awesome","tab_content":"

      Little Italy<\/a>: Where Nancy Pelosi grew up (check out the bocce courts at D\u2019Alesandro Park on Stiles Street--named after her father); super cute neighborhood close to hotel with tons of places to eat, but in particular faves:<\/p>

      Vaccaro\u2019s<\/a>: (0.5 miles) Delicious Italian cookies and pastries. Wheelchair accessible. Menu not accessible.
      Ovenbird<\/a>: (0.6 miles) Bakery with wonderful bread. Wheelchair accessible. Menu not accessible.
      Amicci\u2019s<\/a>: (0.6 miles) Gluten-free pasta options. Lunch and dinner and a great happy hour. Menu accessible.
      Angeli\u2019s Pizzeria<\/a>: (0.7 miles) Vegan and gluten-free pizza options! Lunch and dinner. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.<\/p>

      Forno<\/a>: (0.7 miles) Italian wine bar; good happy hour available Tuesday - Friday 3pm - 6pm at the Bar, Market, & Patio; lunch and dinner. Gluten-free pasta and pizza available. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.<\/p>

      Watersong Yunnan Kitchen<\/a>: (0.9 miles) Hidden gem in the Federal Hill neighborhood. Get the mushrooms and baked tilapia! BYOB. Asian-owned. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.<\/p>

      Lexington Market<\/a>: (1 mile) Since 1782, America\u2019s largest, continuously operating market. Recent renovation opening in fall of 2022, but many of its vendors are still open right now. Including world-famous crab cakes from Faidley\u2019s<\/a>.<\/p>

      Mount Vernon Marketplace<\/a>: (1 mile) A wide variety of restaurants and bars within one building, including The Local Oyster<\/a> featuring the Colossal Crab Sandwich as seen on Netflix. Menu minimally accessible.<\/p>

      Trinacria Foods<\/a>: (1.1 miles) One of the oldest operating Italian delis and run by the same family (opened in 1908), Italian food products for sale including amazing and affordable wine, sandwiches, soup, salads. Great gluten-free options! Best for lunch takeout. Menu accessible.<\/p>

      Cocina Luchadores<\/a>: (1.4 miles) Order at the counter at this family-run restaurant serving Mexican street foods and breakfast items. Menu accessible.<\/p>

      Papi Cuisine<\/a>: (1.5 miles) Caribbean fusion style cuisine and cocktails. Black-owned business. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Wheelchair accessible. Menu not accessible.<\/p>

      Johnny Rad\u2019s<\/a>: (1.5 miles) Artisanal pizza, eclectic pub fare & a variety of beer are offered in casual digs with arcade games by Patterson Park. Vegan friendly. Menu accessible.<\/p>

      Locust Point Steamers (\u201cLP Steamers<\/a>\u201d): (1.7 miles) This seafood joint is informal, affordable, and delicious! Set inside a rowhome, family-owned. Great place to get a dozen crabs and a Natty Boh or two. Rooftop seating available if not too cold. Menu not accessible.<\/p>

      Clavel<\/a>: (3.0 miles) Popular mezcaleria and taqueria located in the Remington neighborhood. Happy Hour is Monday-Friday, 5-7pm; $4 off Margaritas and Queso Fundido (both amazingly delicious). Latine-owned. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Wheelchair accessible. Menu minimally accessible. Pro-tip: get drinks at nearby WC Harlan<\/a> while you wait for your table. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Menu accessible.<\/p>

      Blue Pit BBQ & Whiskey Bar<\/a>: (3.9 miles) Delicious BBQ spot in the Hampden neighborhood. Limited gluten-free, vegan, and vegetarian options. Easy to access via Light Raillink, Woodberry stop. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.<\/p>

      Franchesca's Empanadas Cafe<\/a>: Cafe in Highlandtown neighborhood serving meat and vegan empanadas! Woman-owned. Menu accessible.<\/p>

      Dylan\u2019s Oyster Cellar<\/a>: (4.1 miles) Restaurant in the Hampden neighborhood that offers a fantastic selection of all types of seafood, but they also have a great burger and unique cocktails. Also recommend trying a Baltimore staple, the Coddie (codfish cake, usually served with saltines). Gender-neutral bathrooms. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.

      Koko\u2019s Pub<\/a>: (5.5 miles) Crab cakes! Menu accessible.

      Ekiben<\/a>: (1.1 miles) No-frills Asian spot with a focus on unusual steamed buns, plus bowls & small plates. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Menu accessible.<\/p>","_id":"c2df34f"},{"_id":"a513bd1","tab_title":"Ice Cream","tab_content":"

      The Charmery<\/a>: (various) Lots of locally inspired flavors from this husband and wife team, like Lemon Stick and Old Bay Caramel, along with the classics (and a few dairy-free options). There are multiple locations: the closest to the hotel is 0.8 miles away but open seasonally (wheelchair accessible), and there is another in the Hampden neighborhood open more regularly, 3.6 miles away (gender-neutral bathrooms).<\/p>

      Cajou Creamery<\/a>: (0.9 miles) Only open Friday-Sunday, serves delicious plant-based ice cream. Black-owned business. Vegan. Menu accessible.<\/p>

      Taharka Brothers Ice Cream- R.House<\/a>: (3.6 miles) or Cross Street Market (0.9 miles). Local employee-owned ice cream company that serves amazing small-batch ice cream. Limited vegan options. Majority black-owned business. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.<\/p>

      Bmore Licks<\/a>: (0.6) in Federal Hill or (1.8) miles by Patterson Park. Over 100 flavors of hand-made soft-serve ice cream. Gender-neutral restrooms. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.<\/p>

      Hecho En Baltimore<\/a>: (2.3 miles) for paletas (an amazing Mexican frozen dessert) and products made by local artisans.<\/p>

      Pitango Gelato<\/a>: (.6 mi) in Federal Hill; made on premises gelato and sorbet desserts. Well worth the short walk. <\/p>"}],"__globals__":{"tab_color":"globals\/colors?id=secondary","tab_active_color":"globals\/colors?id=nvc2","content_color":"globals\/colors?id=secondary"},"tabs_align_horizontal":"stretch","tab_typography_typography":"custom","tab_typography_font_family":"Montserrat","tab_typography_font_size":{"unit":"px","size":"22","sizes":[]},"tab_typography_font_weight":"700","content_typography_typography":"custom","content_typography_font_family":"Montserrat","content_typography_font_weight":"500"},"elements":[],"widgetType":"tabs"},{"id":"43f8cb58","elType":"widget","settings":{"space":{"unit":"px","size":"25","sizes":[]}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"spacer"},{"id":"e9fc985","elType":"widget","settings":{"title":"Where to Drink","size":"xl","header_size":"h3","align":"center","__globals__":{"title_color":"globals\/colors?id=nvtextcolor"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"heading"},{"id":"458e5641","elType":"widget","settings":{"width":{"unit":"px","size":"80","sizes":[]},"text":"Divider","weight":{"unit":"px","size":"3","sizes":[]},"align":"center","align_mobile":"left","neb_content_protection_password_placeholder":"Enter Password","neb_content_protection_password_submit_btn_txt":"Submit","__globals__":{"color":"globals\/colors?id=nvtextdarkbg"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"divider"},{"id":"457b1f30","elType":"widget","settings":{"tabs":[{"tab_title":"Coffee","tab_content":"

      Most of the best local coffee places are not near the hotel, but there is a Starbucks inside the hotel.<\/p>

      3 Bean Coffee:<\/a> (0.6 miles) Serves Vagrant coffee. Grab a to-go cup and see the views from nearby Federal Hill Park. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Wheelchair accessible. No online menu.<\/p>

      Ceremony Coffee<\/a>: (0.9 miles at the Cross Street Market<\/a>) Menu not accessible. Grab a breakfast sammy at Steve\u2019s lunch stall while you\u2019re there, a staple of SoBo for the past 50 years, or a cold press juice or smoothie at Gangster Vegan Organics.<\/p>

      Dooby\u2019s<\/a>: (1 mile away) Check out this Korean-inspired cafe in the Mount Vernon neighborhood for breakfast and Passenger coffee. Asian-owned. Gender-neutral restrooms. Wheel-chair accessible. Menu accessible.<\/p>

      Sophomore Coffee<\/a> (2.2 miles away) Small gem of a coffee shop with great espresso. Woman and Black owned. Menu not accessible.<\/p>

      Caf\u00e9 Los Sue\u00f1os<\/a>: (2.8 miles) Cozy coffee shop in the Remington neighborhood. The owner grew up working in the coffee fields of El Salvador and roasts their own beans. No online menu.<\/p>

      Dovecote Cafe<\/a>: (3.0 miles) Gorgeous community-centric cafe in the Reservoir Hill neighborhood with a creative menu and events. Black-owned and women-owned. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Wheelchair accessible. No online menu.<\/p>

      Good Neighbor<\/a>: (4 miles) In Hampden. Great coffee drinks, sandwiches and pastries, along with a curated selection of home goods and kitchen\/bar staples. Amazing and large outdoor space and seating, including Green Neighbor, their plant shop. Gender-neutral restrooms. No online menu.<\/p>

      Artifact Coffee<\/a>: (4 miles) Rustic coffeehouse in a reclaimed factory building serving locally sourced and seasonal light bites. Located in the Hampden\/Woodberry neighborhood near Waverly Brewing, Accessible from Light Raillink Woodberry Stop. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Wheelchair accessible. Menu not accessible.<\/p>","_id":"7740c50"},{"tab_title":"Tea","tab_content":"

      Cuples Tea House<\/a>: (0.9 miles) Open Wednesday to Saturday. Loose-teas and teawares for purchase, along with tea prepared and served in a cozy setting with some prepared sandwiches, pastries, etc. Black\/Woman owned small business. Menu minimally accessible.<\/p>

      Teavolve Cafe<\/a>: (1.1 miles) Harbor East\u2019s favorite cafe to enjoy a colorful menu rich with plant-based and GF options. Black\/Woman owned small business. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Menu not accessible.<\/p>

      Corner Juice Bar<\/a>: (2.0 miles) Open Tuesday to Sunday. Healthy and delicious juices made to order! Order a juice and stroll Patterson Park. Menu accessible.<\/p>","_id":"3ad8496"},{"_id":"635ba62","tab_title":"Breweries","tab_content":"

      A comprehensive guide<\/a><\/p>

      Checkerspot<\/a>: (1.2 miles) Woman-owned and brewed gluten-reduced beers. Dog-friendly. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.<\/p>

      Ministry of Brewing<\/a>: (1.2 miles) Spacious brewery in Upper Fells Point housed in the former St. Michael\u2019s Church. Wheelchair accessible. Menu not accessible.<\/p>

      Suspended Brewing Company<\/a>: (1.2 miles) Women of color-owned vegan, cruelty-free mixed fermentation beers in Pigtown. Wheelchair accessible. Stop by the B&O Railroad Museum while you\u2019re in the area. No online menu.<\/p>

      Charm City Meadworks<\/a>: (1.2 miles) 20 minutes by bus or 7 minutes by car. Large taproom with indoor and outdoor seating serving locally made mead (gluten-free). Bring your own food. Dog-friendly. Gender-neutral bathrooms. Wheelchair accessible. Menu minimally accessible.<\/p>

      Diamondback Brewery<\/a>: (1.9 miles) Unfiltered lagers, hop-forward ales, and mixed fermentation brews. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.<\/p>

      Monument City Brewery<\/a>: (3.0 miles) Well-considered, drinkable ales designed to be a go-to beer choice. Dogs allowed. Wheelchair accessible. Menu accessible.<\/p>"},{"_id":"ecfd500","tab_title":"Bars","tab_content":"

      The Owl Bar<\/a> inside the Belvedere Hotel (on the first floor): (1.3 miles) a favorite of H.L. Menken and F. Scott Fitzgerald and other celebrities of their day. A quote from Fitzgerald on Baltimore: \"I belong here, where everything is civilized and gay and rotted and polite.\" Menu minimally accessible.<\/p>

      Sugarvale<\/a> (1 mile): A cozy cocktail bar in the Mount Vernon neighborhood with great ambience. Limited indoor seating and vaccination cards required. Gender-neutral restrooms. Menu not accessible.<\/p>

      Fadensonnen<\/a>: (2.2 miles) 20 minutes by bus or 11 minutes by car. An upscale beer garden and tavern in the artsy Station North neighborhood focusing on ethically produced beer, wine, nihonshu, and shochu. Generous outdoor seating. Women-owned. Gender-neutral restrooms. Menu accessible.<\/p>

      Dutch Courage<\/a>: (2.2 miles) Fantastic gin bar and a great back up if Fadensonnen is crowded. Menu not accessible.<\/p>

      WC Harlan<\/a>: (3 miles) Bar in Remington serving speakeasy style cocktails and drinks. Note: There is no sign, search for the black door that has \u201cEnter\u201d written in chalk. Gender-neutral restrooms. Menu accessible.<\/p>

      Club Charles<\/a>: (aka Club Chuck) (2.2. miles) One of John Waters\u2019 favorites, a divine divey bar with a jukebox, cheap drinks, and fun bathroom graffiti. Menu not available.<\/p>

      Bluebird Cocktail Room<\/a>: (4.0 miles) Romantic, literary-themed cocktail bar in the Hampden neighborhood. Gender-neutral restrooms. Menu not accessible.<\/p>

      Melanie\u2019s at Griffith\u2019s Tavern<\/a>: (4.0 miles) LGBTQ and women owned Hampden neighborhood dive bar with reasonably priced drinks. Menu not available. <\/p>"}],"tabs_align_horizontal":"stretch","tab_typography_typography":"custom","tab_typography_font_family":"Montserrat","tab_typography_font_size":{"unit":"px","size":"22","sizes":[]},"tab_typography_font_weight":"700","content_typography_typography":"custom","content_typography_font_family":"Montserrat","content_typography_font_weight":"500","__globals__":{"tab_color":"globals\/colors?id=secondary","tab_active_color":"globals\/colors?id=nvc2","content_color":"globals\/colors?id=secondary"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"tabs"},{"id":"38feab8","elType":"widget","settings":{"space":{"unit":"px","size":"25","sizes":[]}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"spacer"},{"id":"559731d4","elType":"widget","settings":{"title":"Where to Visit","size":"xl","header_size":"h3","align":"center","__globals__":{"title_color":"globals\/colors?id=nvtextcolor"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"heading"},{"id":"1bbf7ae2","elType":"widget","settings":{"width":{"unit":"px","size":"80","sizes":[]},"text":"Divider","weight":{"unit":"px","size":"3","sizes":[]},"align":"center","align_mobile":"left","neb_content_protection_password_placeholder":"Enter Password","neb_content_protection_password_submit_btn_txt":"Submit","__globals__":{"color":"globals\/colors?id=nvtextdarkbg"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"divider"}],"isInner":""}],"isInner":""},{"id":"230a7584","elType":"section","settings":[],"elements":[{"id":"11e308e2","elType":"column","settings":{"_column_size":"100"},"elements":[{"id":"70332e3a","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

      Since you\u2019re at the Inner Harbor<\/span>, visit the National Aquarium<\/a> (wheelchair accessible), Turtle Island<\/a>, and local celebrity Mr. Trash Wheel<\/a> at his home 0.6 miles away<\/a>. This googly eyed genius keeps our bay clean and encourages recycling. Tag him on social media (seriously his Instagram is one of the best). He is related to Professor Trash Wheel, Captain Trash Wheel, and Gwynnda the Good Wheel of the West, but he was the first. He has also partnered with local brewery Peabody Heights on 3 beers<\/a>, Solar Power Sour, Lost Python Ale (from that time when a python came to visit<\/a> with the trash), and Professor Trash Wheel Blinded Me With Science.<\/p>

      See the Reginald F. Lewis Museum of African American History<\/a> (0.4 miles) and The National Great Blacks in Wax Museum<\/a> (2.5 miles)<\/p>

      See Edgar Allen Poe\u2019s grave<\/a> (0.9 miles) at 515 W Fayette St, a 17-minute walk; open during the day, and then go see his house<\/a> and museum (1.5 miles). The house is not wheel-chair accessible but the museum is.<\/p>

      Jewish Museum of Maryland<\/a>: (0.7 miles) near Attman\u2019s Deli<\/a> and includes historic Lloyd Street Synagogue. Get corned beef on Corned Beef Row at Attman\u2019s Deli for lunch.<\/p>

      See outsider art at the American Visionary Art Museum<\/a> (1.2 miles) and some amazing letter presses at the Baltimore Museum of Industry<\/a>, located in a former oyster cannery (1.5 miles). Grab some seafood at nearby LP Steamers and a beer at Diamondback brewery. Both wheelchair accessible.<\/p>

      For fine and contemporary art, visit the Walters<\/a> (0.9 miles) and the Baltimore Museum of Art<\/a> (3.0 miles), both free and conveniently located along the Light Rail. Both wheelchair accessible. For local galleries, Galerie Myrtis<\/a> (2.1 miles) is Black, woman-owned blue-chip gallery specializing in twentieth and twenty-first-century American art with a focus on work created by African American artists.<\/p>

      For a bibliophile tour, visit the Enoch Pratt Free Library (0.8 miles), the recently renovated central branch, as well as the George Peabody Library<\/a> (0.9 miles). Known as Baltimore\u2019s \u201cCathedral of Books,\u201d Peabody is consistently ranked among the most beautiful libraries in the world. If it happens to be the one day of the month that Book Thing<\/a> (2.9 miles) is open, trek up to Charles Village to pick up some free collaging gems. All wheelchair accessible. Nearby is worker-owned Red Emma\u2019s Bookstore Coffeehouse<\/a> and Normals Books & Records<\/a>.<\/p>","typography_typography":"custom","typography_font_family":"Montserrat","typography_font_weight":"500","__globals__":{"text_color":"globals\/colors?id=secondary"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"text-editor"},{"id":"253aaa61","elType":"widget","settings":{"title":"What to Do","size":"xl","header_size":"h3","align":"center","__globals__":{"title_color":"globals\/colors?id=nvtextcolor"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"heading"},{"id":"2b91cdba","elType":"widget","settings":{"width":{"unit":"px","size":"80","sizes":[]},"text":"Divider","weight":{"unit":"px","size":"3","sizes":[]},"align":"center","align_mobile":"left","neb_content_protection_password_placeholder":"Enter Password","neb_content_protection_password_submit_btn_txt":"Submit","__globals__":{"color":"globals\/colors?id=nvtextdarkbg"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"divider"},{"id":"37696eb3","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"

      Stroll along the Promenade - the brick route along the Baltimore Harbor. Head toward Federal Hill (to the right when you\u2019re facing the water and the hotel is at your back) or Fells Point and Canton (to the left). There\u2019s a pleasant path along the water for several miles in each direction from the hotel. Most parts of the Promenade are wheelchair, bike, and stroller accessible. Learn more about the Promenade and view maps on the Baltimore City website<\/a>.<\/p>

      Go on a Saturday morning to the Waverly Farmer\u2019s Market<\/a> or on a Sunday morning to the Baltimore Farmers Market<\/a> under I-83. See the Hollywood Diner<\/a> from the Barry Levinson movies \u201cDiner\u201d and \u201cTin Men\u201d (0.5 miles) at Holliday and Saratoga Sts.: not a restaurant anymore. See it in the 1980s<\/a> as the Kids Diner.<\/p>

      See a performance at Le Mondo<\/a> (0.9 miles), an artist-owned bar and event venue with avant-garde concerts, dance, and theatrical performances.<\/p>

      Follow in the footsteps<\/a> of Frederick Douglass around Fells Point. Do a Fells Point ghost tour<\/a> (1.2 miles) and get some mussels and live music at Bertha\u2019s<\/a> across the street. Pick up the water taxi at the Fell\u2019s Point pier for a cruise around the harbor (make sure to check out their hours<\/a> since it's off season).<\/p>

      Do some Duckpin bowling at Patterson Bowling Center<\/a>: (1.4 miles) and BYOB (Pro tip: bring a 6-pack of local brewery Union\u2019s Duckpin Pale Ale<\/a> or a pizza from Johnny Rad\u2019s<\/a> across the street)! Duckpin is like regular bowling, only smaller pins and balls, and slightly different rules\u2013so actually, it\u2019s pretty different. Afterwards visit Patterson Park<\/a> and then go see some local art at Creative Alliance<\/a> and shop at Hecho En Baltimore<\/a> (2.3 miles) for paletas and products made by local artisans.<\/p>

      Shake and Bake Family Fun Center<\/a>: (2.2 miles) Baltimore City Recreation and Parks (BCRP) owns and operates the Shake & Bake Family Fun Center in the historic Upton community in West Baltimore. \u201cThe Bake\u201d as it is affectionately known, has been a local, iconic staple since 1982. Named after Baltimore Colts wide receiver, Glenn \u201cShake & Bake'' Doughty. Shake & Bake is the spot for Bowling and Roller Skating under one roof in the heart of Baltimore City! This link<\/a> leads to a short video on PBS about Shake & Bake.<\/p>

      See a show at Ottobar<\/a> (2.6 miles) and stop by Beyond Video<\/a> while you\u2019re in the neighborhood, nonprofit video rental store in a row home.<\/p>

      Peruse The Avenue in Hampden (3.7 miles), which is technically named W. 36th Street. Also Hampden is pronounced HAM-din. Tons of great shops (including vintage), restaurants, and bars as well as Atomic Books<\/a>, an independent bookstore where John Waters gets his fan mail. Pro-tip: watch John Waters\u2019 PECKER (1998) beforehand which takes place almost entirely in Hampden.<\/p>

      Lithuanian Hall<\/a>: (1.2 miles) Save Your Soul is a monthly dance party featuring the best Dj's spinning the rarest and rawest Soul, RnB, and Boogaloo 45's on the first Friday of every month at the historic Lithuanian Hall in Baltimore. Try a shot of the traditional honey liqueur, Krupnikas<\/p>

      There are a plethora of hiking trails in and around the Baltimore area for all levels. Local favorites include the Cascade Falls Trail<\/a> in Patapsco Valley State Park (21 minutes by car), the Merryman\u2019s Mill Trail<\/a> at the Loch Raven Reservoir (27 mins by car), and the Leakin Park Loop Trail<\/a> up to the Orianda Mansion (21 minutes by car).<\/p>

      Baltimore has a number of lovely parks. Local favorites include Federal Hill Park (1 mile), Patterson Park (2.3 miles), Druid Hill (4 miles) and Clifton Park (3.1 miles). item.title: 2022 sponsorship page
item.dc:creator: gschechter
item.content:encoded:
Sponsorship

Our 2022 sponsorship opportunities are closed,
but reach out to us about supporting the 2023 CLIR events.

Connect your brand to a multi-disciplinary cross-sector audience of professionals in the digital library, museum, archives, and cultural heritage fields, from project managers, technologists, and developers to administrators and service providers.

Sponsor the 2023 Events

Download the Sponsorship Pack

View the Sponsorship Pack in your browser

Meet our 2022 Sponsors

Who and What to Expect at Our Events

We are thrilled to invite you to join us as a sponsor at the 2022 Digital Library Federation (DLF) Forum, Learn@DLF pre-conference, NDSA’s Digital Preservation, and the Digitizing Hidden Collections (DHC) Symposium on October 9-13 in Baltimore, Maryland.

These events are multi-day experiences for learning, networking, and skill-building, working to inspire, connect, and share successes and failures with a dedicated community of digital library practitioners. After two years of meeting online due to the pandemic, we are eager to host a safe, inclusive, in-person event in Baltimore, MD, based on the guiding principle of gratitude.

Sponsoring the DLF Forum connects your brand to a multi-disciplinary cross-sector audience of professionals in the digital library, museum, archives, and cultural heritage fields, from project managers, technologists, and developers to administrators and service providers. The Forum has welcomed professionals from academic, art and cultural heritage, and non-profit organizations, government agencies, and more.

The DLF Forum convenes a community of deeply engaged, hands-on professionals seeking actionable and informative insights to inform decisions for their organizations. With over 20 years of Forum organizing experience, we know what it takes to drive value for our sponsors.

While the Forum is open to all, DLF has a robust membership community, consisting of over 160 organizations. Take advantage of the opportunity to meet this engaged community where they come together across these simultaneous events.

DLF Forum with Learn@DLF Pre-Conference – October 9-12
Annual In-Person Attendance: over 600
The Forum kicks off on October 9 with the pre-conference Learn@DLF featuring hands-on workshops for attendees to learn new tools and exchange ideas with fellow community members. The Forum will follow on October 10-12 where professionals from academic, art, cultural heritage, non-profit organizations, and government agencies from around the country and abroad connect, collaborate, and share their work and experiences.

NDSA’s Digital Preservation – October 12-13
Annual In-Person Attendance: 200
The Digital Preservation conference is the meeting place for NDSA’s 260+ partnering organizations and is a venue for intellectual exchange, community-building, development of good practices, and national-level agenda-setting in the digital stewardship field.

Digitizing Hidden Collections Symposium – October 12-13
Anticipated Attendance: 300
This symposium will invite grant recipients of CLIR’s Digitizing Hidden Special Collections and Archives grant program to build on their collective experiences and reflect on how the digital cultural record can better reflect the diversity of human thought and experience, how law and ethics affect strategies for access, and how technologies and standards can improve discovery and learning.

Check out our sponsorship levels and please don’t hesitate to contact us at forum@diglib.org if you have any questions. Thank you for your consideration in supporting these exciting events!

Sponsorship Levels and Included Benefits

We have a variety of sponsorship opportunities to engage with attendees of the DLF Forum and affiliated events. Check out our tiered levels, add-ons, and unique opportunities. We are always happy to discuss custom sponsorship packages as well so please reach out to forum@diglib.org.

Please note that exhibitor tables require Silver level sponsorship or higher. Exhibitors engage with attendees to make connections and have meaningful conversations. Speak directly to decision makers and other professionals in the industry. Limited space is available, so reserve your spot soon!

Have you sponsored previously? If yes, we’re excited to offer you a 25% discount on any sponsorship level. New sponsors that are a non-profit, educational, or organizations with fewer than 10 full time employees also receive a 25% discount on any sponsorship level.

Download the Sponsorship Pack

Standard Benefits for All Levels

  • Company name on the Forum website
  • Acknowledgement from the podium during plenaries
  • Logo on digital screens in conference hotel
  • Social media mentions

Platinum

2 OF 3 REMAINING $ 7,000
  • In addition to all standard benefits, Platinum sponsorship includes:
  • Named signature event sponsor for the DLF Forum reception, keynote, or closing session
  • Exhibitor table
  • Featured sponsor blog post on Forum website
  • Company logo and about text on Forum website
  • Opted-in attendee email addresses
  • 3 tickets to CLIR events of your choosing
  • Company logo on pocket schedule
  • Company name on pocket schedule
  • 9 social media mentions
  • 3 custom banners in event emails
Be a Platinum Sponsor

Gold

4 OF 10 REMAINING $ 5,000
  • In addition to all standard benefits, Gold sponsorship includes:
  • Named sponsor for one breakfast or lunch during the Forum or affiliated events
  • Exhibitor table
  • Featured sponsor blog post on Forum website
  • Company logo and about text on Forum website
  • Opted-in attendee email addresses
  • 2 tickets to CLIR events of your choosing
  • Company logo on pocket schedule
  • Company name on pocket schedule
  • 7 social media mentions
  • 2 custom banners in event emails
Be a Gold Sponsor

Silver

$ 2,500
  • In addition to all standard benefits, Silver sponsorship includes:
  • Exhibitor table
  • Company logo and about text on Forum website
  • Opted-in attendee email addresses
  • 1 ticket to a CLIR event of your choosing
  • Company name on pocket schedule
  • 5 social media mentions
  • 1 custom banner in event emails
Be a Silver Sponsor

Bronze

$ 1,000
  • In addition to all standard benefits, Bronze sponsorship includes:
  • 3 social media mentions
Be a Bronze Sponsor

Add-Ons and Unique Opportunities

Coffee Break Add-On

(4 of 8 remaining)
$500

Help us keep attendees caffeinated by adding on a coffee break to any sponsorship level or opportunity listed. Attendees will appreciate it! Coffee break opportunities are available across all events and are first-come, first-served, so commit to sponsoring soon to get your preferred break.

Forum Livestream


$7,000

The webcast and recording of select sessions will extend the conversation beyond the conference. Includes all the benefits of a Platinum level sponsorship, except for a named signature event. Your company’s name would be associated with all mentions of the livestream in lieu of a named signature event.

DHC Symposium Keynote


$3,000

Support an important voice in the field of digitizing cultural heritage collections by sponsoring the Digitizing Hidden Collections Symposium keynote address. Your company will name this signature event popular with attendees. Includes all benefits of a Silver level sponsorship.

Swag Sponsor


CLAIMED

Your logo will appear alongside DLF’s on the official conference swag that attendees can opt-in to receive. The type of swag will be determined with Forum staff who welcome your ideas on fun items we could offer to attendees. Includes all the benefits of a Gold level sponsorship.

Badge Lanyards

CLAIMED

All conference attendees will be wearing your logo all five days of the events, and in photos from the conference. Includes all the benefits of a Silver level sponsorship. 

Forum Fellowships

(1 of 2 available)
$2,500

Support inclusivity at the DLF Forum by helping us bring new and engaged professionals to the three-day event. Your company will be thanked in the Fellowship section of our website and at the end of every fellows’ blog post for the DLF website. Includes all benefits of a Silver level sponsorship. Take a look at our fellowship opportunities.

Custom Package

Collaborate with DLF staff to select benefits that will highlight your company in the best way for you and demonstrate your commitment to the DLF community. Contact forum@diglib.org to discuss custom sponsorship needs.

We are thrilled to invite you to join us as a sponsor at the 2022 <\/span>Digital Library Federation (DLF) Forum<\/b>, Learn@DLF<\/strong> pre-conference, <\/span>NDSA\u2019s Digital Preservation<\/b>, and the <\/span>Digitizing Hidden Collections (DHC) Symposium<\/b> on October 9-13 in Baltimore, Maryland.<\/span><\/p>

These events are multi-day experiences for learning, networking, and skill-building, working to inspire, connect, and share successes and failures with a dedicated community of digital library practitioners. After two years of meeting online due to the pandemic, we are eager to host a safe, inclusive, in-person event in Baltimore, MD, based on the guiding principle of gratitude.<\/span><\/p>

Sponsoring the DLF Forum connects your brand to a multi-disciplinary cross-sector audience of professionals in the digital library, museum, archives, and cultural heritage fields, from project managers, technologists, and developers to administrators and service providers. The Forum has welcomed professionals from academic, art and cultural heritage, and non-profit organizations, government agencies, and more.<\/span><\/p>

The DLF Forum convenes a community of deeply engaged, hands-on professionals seeking actionable and informative insights to inform decisions for their organizations. With over 20 years of Forum organizing experience, we know what it takes to drive value for our sponsors.<\/span><\/p>

While the Forum is open to all, DLF has a robust <\/span>membership community<\/span><\/a>, consisting of over 160 organizations. Take advantage of the opportunity to meet this engaged community where they come together across these simultaneous events.<\/span><\/p>

DLF Forum<\/a> with Learn@DLF<\/a> Pre-Conference<\/strong> - October 9-12
Annual In-Person Attendance: over 600<\/em>
The Forum kicks off on October 9 with the pre-conference Learn@DLF featuring hands-on workshops for attendees to learn new tools and exchange ideas with fellow community members. The Forum will follow on October 10-12 where professionals from academic, art, cultural heritage, non-profit organizations, and government agencies from around the country and abroad connect, collaborate, and share their work and experiences.<\/p>

NDSA\u2019s Digital Preservation<\/strong> <\/a>- October 12-13
Annual In-Person Attendance: 200<\/em>
The Digital Preservation conference is the meeting place for NDSA\u2019s 260+ partnering organizations and is a venue for intellectual exchange, community-building, development of good practices, and national-level agenda-setting in the digital stewardship field.<\/p>

Digitizing Hidden Collections Symposium<\/strong><\/a> - October 12-13
Anticipated Attendance: 300<\/em>
This symposium will invite grant recipients of CLIR\u2019s Digitizing Hidden Special Collections and Archives grant program to build on their collective experiences and reflect on how the digital cultural record can better reflect the diversity of human thought and experience, how law and ethics affect strategies for access, and how technologies and standards can improve discovery and learning.<\/p>

Check out our sponsorship levels and please don\u2019t hesitate to contact us at <\/span>forum@diglib.org<\/span><\/a> if you have any questions. Thank you for your consideration in supporting these exciting events!<\/span><\/p>","_id":"8d3c087"}],"selected_icon":{"value":"fas fa-chevron-down","library":"fa-solid"},"selected_active_icon":{"value":"fas fa-chevron-up","library":"fa-solid"},"title_typography_typography":"custom","title_typography_font_family":"Montserrat","title_typography_font_size":{"unit":"px","size":"26","sizes":[]},"title_typography_font_weight":"600","__globals__":{"title_color":"globals\/colors?id=nvtextcolor","tab_active_color":"globals\/colors?id=nvtextcolor","content_color":"globals\/colors?id=nvtextcolor","border_color":"globals\/colors?id=nvsecondaryaccent"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"accordion"},{"id":"69162fee","elType":"widget","settings":[],"elements":[],"widgetType":"spacer"},{"id":"66d26d4c","elType":"widget","settings":{"title":"Sponsorship Levels and Included Benefits","size":"xl","__globals__":{"title_color":"globals\/colors?id=nvtextcolor"}},"elements":[],"widgetType":"heading"},{"id":"4fadfab9","elType":"widget","settings":{"editor":"
